attributes.body_ja:
助動詞（じょどうし）の「べき」は「べし」の連体形（れんたいけい）で、主（おも）に動詞（どうし）に付（つ）けて使（つか）われます。意味（いみ）は「(A) をしなければならない」です。この文法（ぶんぽう）には「(A) をするのが当（あ）たり前（まえ）だ」や「(A) だけが適切（てきせつ）な行動（こうどう）だ」のようなニュアンスがあります。また、この文法（ぶんぽう）には「良（よ）いと許（ゆる）す」などの意味（いみ）を持（も）つ漢字（かんじ）の「可（べ）き」が当（あ）てられています（(A) 以外（いがい）のほかの行動（こうどう）は認（みと）められないことを示（しめ）します）。

「べき」は、動詞（どうし）の辞書形（じしょけい）に付（つ）きます。そのあとに、「だ」や別（べつ）の名詞（めいし）が続（つづ）きます。

「べき」は、(A) だけが正（ただ）しいと話（はな）し手（て）が思（おも）っているときに使（つか）われる、強（つよ）い表現（ひょうげん）です。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「べき」を使（つか）って過去（かこ）のことを言（い）いたいときは、「べき」のあとに「だった」や「でした」を付（つ）けます。「べき」の前（まえ）の動詞（どうし）が、過去形（かこけい）になるのではありません。注意（ちゅうい）しましょう。

豆知識（まめちしき）

現代（げんだい）の日本語（にほんご）には、助動詞（じょどうし）が１８種類（しゅるい）ありますが、「べき」はその中（なか）に入（はい）っていません。「べき」や「べし」は、古文（こぶん）の助動詞（じょどうし）（文語助動詞（ぶんごじょどうし））とされています。

豆知識（まめちしき）

動詞（どうし）の「する」を「べき」とつなぐ場合（ばあい）は、「するべき」と「すべき」のどちらの形（かたち）も正（ただ）しいとされています。
attributes.body:
The auxiliary verb べき, being the attributive form of べし, is a structure in Japanese that is often paired with verbs to express that something 'ought to be done'. It implies some sort of moral obligation, or that (A) is the only reasonable course of action. This comes from the kanji 可（べ）き, which carries the meaning of being something 'permissible' (indicating that any other action would not be acceptable).

べき will be paired with the plain (non-past) form of a verb, before being followed by either だ, or another noun.

べき is also sometimes translated as 'must do (A)', or 'should do (A)' but it is important to remember that it will always have the nuance of being the only 'permissible' choice, and is therefore very strong.

Caution

It is important to note that the verb appearing with べき cannot be in past tense, and you will need to use だった or でした after べき, if you would like to say that something 'ought to have been done' in the past.

Fun Fact

In modern Japanese, there are only 18 auxiliary verbs, of which べき is not one. べし (the standard form) is considered to be a classical auxiliary verb. Due to this, べき (and べし) are often referred to as classical auxiliary verbs.

Fun Fact

The combination of する and べき is a rare grammatical exception in Japanese, in which two forms are both considered equally correct. Due to this, either するべき, or すべき may be used.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: Using 「べき」 to describe actions one should do
接続・意味・使い方・例文

attributes.body: Both expressions are similar in that they are both derived from the classical Japanese べし and relate to expectations, but they differ in precise meaning. べく typically expresses an action performed for a particular purpose, e.g. 上達すべく毎日練習しています ('I practice every day in hopes of getting better.'), while べき expresses a societal expectation in the sense of saying that something is how it 'should' be, e.g. 言いたいことがある時は本人に言うべきです ('When you have something to say, you should tell the person concerned.')

first_relatable.title: べく
first_relatable.meaning: For the purpose of, In order to, To ensure

attributes.body: べき expresses strong obligation or moral judgment, as in doing something because it is right or proper, e.g. 約束は守るべきだ ('You should keep your promises.') べきではない is the negative form, used to advise against actions considered wrong or inappropriate, e.g. 人を見た目で判断すべきではない ('You shouldn't judge people by appearances.')

first_relatable.title: べきではない
first_relatable.meaning: Should not, Must not , Ought not to

attributes.body: ないと and べき both express a sense of necessity, but with different nuances. ないと focuses on immediate or practical obligation, like 行かないと ('I've got to go.'). べき expresses moral or logical duty, as in 行くべきだ ('You should go.').

Both express obligation, but differ in tone. ことだ is used to offer advice or general suggestions, e.g. 無理をしないことだ ('You should take it easy.') べき is stronger, implying moral or logical necessity, e.g. 約束は守るべきだ ('You should keep your promises.')

Both express what one 'should' do, but with different nuance. べき reflects personal or moral judgment, e.g. 約束は守るべきだ ('You should keep your promises.') ものだ conveys social or cultural expectations, e.g. 子どもは早く寝るものだ ('Children are supposed to go to bed early.')

first_relatable.title: ものだ
first_relatable.meaning: Supposed to, Should, That's the way it is

attributes.body: はずだ and べき can both be translated as 'should', but they differ in nuance. はずだ expresses an expectation based on evidence or reasoning, like 明日来るはずだ ('He should come tomorrow.'). In contrast, べき expresses obligation or social correctness, as in 来るべきだ ('You should come.').

first_relatable.title: はずだ
first_relatable.meaning: Bound to (be), Expected to (be), Should be (able)

attributes.body: ないほうがいい is used to advise against doing something, similar 'You shouldn't…' in English. It is a common expression that reflects the speaker's personal or subjective opinion. べき has the opposite meaning ('You should,') and is more formal. It carries the nuance of stating what 'ought to' be done based on social norms, rather than giving personal judgment or advice.

first_relatable.title: ないほうがいい
first_relatable.meaning: It'd be better not to, Shouldn't do

attributes.body: たほうがいい is used to give advice or make a suggestion, often expressing the speaker's subjective opinion on what they believe would be better. It's commonly used in everyday conversation. べき has a similar meaning, but is more formal and has a stronger nuance of expectation about what 'should' be done, rather than a personal opinion.

first_relatable.title: たほうがいい
first_relatable.meaning: It'd be better to, Should do
